title: Telemetry-driven dataset pruner for eval runners to improve profile fidelity
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Objective: Reduce noise in generated performance profiles by pruning low-signal dataset slices automatically using live eval-runner telemetry. The goal is to produce more stable, representative profiles at publish time so that model pinning and rollout decisions rely on higher fidelity metrics.

Background: Current profile generation pipelines ingest large dataset catalogs and prompt variants uniformly which frequently includes low-volume slices or data patterns that exacerbate variance in latency and quality metrics. Onboarded models then get pinned with profiles that oscillate when these low-signal slices appear in subsequent runs. Engineers and PMs have asked for an automated, data-driven step to reduce this instability without manual curator intervention.

Scope: Implement an eval-runner-side pruning service and a pipeline integration that: 1) collects lightweight telemetry (sample counts, avg latency, token distribution, metric variance per slice); 2) computes a per-slice signal score and flags low-signal slices; 3) prunes or de-prioritizes flagged slices for profile synthesis; 4) persists pruning decisions and rationale in the profile metadata for auditability. This ticket covers the core runner-side telemetry hooks, the prune-scoring algorithm, profile metadata extension, basic dashboarding for verification, and a canary publish workflow.

Design decisions and trade-offs considered: 1) Telemetry granularity: we sample per-run aggregated metrics rather than full per-request logs to limit cost and PII exposure. 2) Scoring heuristic: combine sample_count, variance (stderr) on quality metrics, and latency outlier rate into a weighted signal score. We chose a heuristic approach first for speed; a later follow-up will explore an ML classifier if heuristics prove brittle. 3) Pruning policy: default "soft-prune" (de-prioritize and reduce sampling probability) rather than hard removal to avoid blind spots. 4) Auditability: every pruning decision is stored with a compact rationale string and telemetry snapshot.

Implementation tasks: 
- Add runner telemetry hooks: sample_count, mean_latency_ms, token_histogram_summary, quality_metric_mean, quality_metric_stddev (Markus)
- Implement prune-scoring module and config (weighting knobs) (Markus/Aisha)
- Extend profile manifest schema: pruned_slices[], prune_rationale[], prune_timestamp (metadata string fields) (Design/PM review)
- Integrate pruning step into profile generator; ensure deterministic seeding for reproducible prunes in CI (Samira will help with deterministic pseudo-random)
- Add console dashboard tiles: pruned slice list, before/after profile variance graphs, and sampling rate changes (BI/Console)
- Canary pipeline: publish pruned-profile to a "canary" namespace and run 500 synthetic runs with historical seeds to validate stability improvements before promoting to prod profiles (QA/CI)

Acceptance criteria: 
- Runner emits telemetry in compressed JSON lines to the profile pipeline for >=95% of eval runs in the canary cohort.
- The prune-scoring module exposes config flags for thresholds and weights and tests demonstrating expected behavior on toy datasets.
- Profile manifests produced after pruning include pruned_slices and prune_rationale fields; downstream consumers ignore pruned slices by default.
- Canary validation shows >=20% reduction in cross-run metric variance for target quality/latency metrics on at least 3 models of varying sizes.
- Documentation updated: README for pruning logic, how to tune weights, and audit log access.

Dependencies: 
- ENG-412854 (adaptive-probe-guided-sample-pruner) conceptual overlap — coordinate to avoid duplicate logic.
- Console team PR for dashboard tiles and RBAC for canary profiles.
- CI infra change to allow seeding synthetic runs (ENG-130999 referenced for earlier microbench refactor).

Risks and mitigations: 
- Risk: Pruning could remove rare but critical edge-case slices that later surface in production. Mitigation: soft-prune default and retention of pruned slices in metadata; allow manual un-prune via profile UI.
- Risk: Telemetry adds overhead. Mitigation: telemetry is aggregated and sampled; profiling shows <1% CPU/latency overhead in local tests.

Rollout plan: 
1) Feature flagged merge to main with runner telemetry off by default. 
2) Enable telemetry in internal canary org and run 2-week data collection. 
3) Iterate scoring weights and publish canary pruned profiles. 
4) Run validation benchmark suite; if metrics improve and no regressions, enable soft-prune for public profile generation for scaffolded customers. 
5) Monitor for 4 weeks, then consider aggressive prune thresholds as opt-in.

Metrics to track: 
- % of slices flagged pruned and their cumulative sample share.
- Cross-run stddev of quality metrics pre/post prune.
- False-positive edge-case discovery rate (incidents tied to pruned slices).
- Runtime overhead of telemetry (p50 and p95).

Follow-ups: 
- Build ML-based classifier for low-signal detection (future ticket).
- Add automatic rollback triggers if canary shows customer-impacting regressions.
